clinicalPearls: Characterised by symmetric, non-encapsulated masses of adipose tissue around the neck, shoulders, and upper trunk, producing a 'horse-collar' or pseudoathletic appearance
Predominantly affects middle-aged men and is strongly associated with chronic heavy alcohol use
Distinct from lipodystrophy in that fat accumulates abnormally rather than being lost, though the lower limbs may appear relatively fat-depleted
Some cases are linked to mitochondrial dysfunction (including MERRF-associated mutations), suggesting impaired brown-fat metabolism
The accumulating tissue resembles brown adipose tissue with defective catecholamine-driven lipolysis
Neck and mediastinal fat deposition can cause compressive symptoms such as dysphagia, dyspnoea, or airway compromise
An associated peripheral or autonomic neuropathy is common, and metabolic disturbances including insulin resistance may coexist
Diagnosis rests on the characteristic symmetric fat distribution and imaging; alcohol cessation is advised and debulking surgery is used for compression or cosmesis
reference.pathophysiology: Madelung disease is a disorder of abnormal proliferation and accumulation of adipose tissue in a symmetric distribution around the neck, nape, shoulders, and upper trunk. The affected fat has features of brown adipose tissue with impaired catecholamine-stimulated lipolysis, so it expands unchecked rather than being mobilised. Mitochondrial dysfunction, including mutations associated with MERRF and heavy alcohol exposure, is implicated in disrupting normal adipocyte metabolism. Unlike the lipodystrophies, the primary problem is pathological fat gain in specific depots; the growing masses are cosmetically disfiguring and can compress the airway, oesophagus, and vascular structures, while an associated neuropathy and metabolic disturbance may accompany the condition.
additionalDifferentials: Cushing syndrome (dorsocervical and supraclavicular fat pads)
additionalInvestigations: CT or MRI of the neck and thorax to map fat deposits and assess compression
Liver function tests and markers reflecting chronic alcohol use
Fasting glucose/HbA1c and lipid profile for associated metabolic disturbance
Nerve conduction studies if neuropathy is suspected
Evaluation for mitochondrial disease where clinically indicated
Cortisol testing to exclude Cushing syndrome when the picture is ambiguous
redFlags: Airway compromise, stridor, or dyspnoea from cervical/mediastinal fat
Rapid growth or atypical features raising concern for malignancy
Superior vena cava or vascular compression
reference.prognosis: Madelung disease is benign but often progressive and disfiguring; alcohol cessation may slow growth, and surgical debulking relieves compression and improves appearance, though recurrence is common and any associated neuropathy or metabolic disease persists.
pitfalls: Mistaking the fat distribution for Cushing syndrome or simple obesity
Overlooking airway or oesophageal compression from neck deposits
Failing to recognise the strong association with chronic alcohol use
Assuming the masses are discrete encapsulated lipomas amenable to simple excision
Missing an associated neuropathy or mitochondrial disorder
references: Endocrine Society clinical practice guidance on disorders of adipose tissue
management: Alcohol abstinence is central, as cessation may slow progression and reduce recurrence, with structured support for alcohol-use disorder
Surgical debulking by lipectomy or liposuction to relieve compression of the airway, oesophagus and vessels and to improve appearance
Urgent surgical decompression for compressive complications such as airway compromise, dysphagia or dyspnoea
Manage associated metabolic disturbance and comorbidity, including glucose and lipid control and correction of alcohol-related liver and nutritional deficiency
Symptomatic treatment of the associated peripheral and autonomic neuropathy
Investigation for mitochondrial disease where clinically indicated, with appropriate counselling
Multidisciplinary care across surgery, endocrinology and addiction services, with counselling that recurrence is common after debulking
